qt: to the Commission Theodoros Zagorakis (NI) Subject:

The provision of first aid plays an exceptionally important role in the rapid response to emergencies and accidents and can literally save lives. However, there is little instruction or awareness-raising. The absence of a uniform training plan becomes even more apparent if we compare the different approaches taken by Member States. On the basis of the above and my previous question Ε-008747-151: 1.
Does the Commission have detailed data on first-aid training for citizens, and if so, what is the situation in Greece?

How does it plan to raise awareness among citizens and give them incentives to take appropriate training, and what financial tools can be made available to promote similar education in school curricula?
How does the Commission intend to standardise first-aid training methods in Member States with the aim of ensuring the highest possible quality?
at: (English version) to the Commission Theodoros Zagorakis (NI) (2 April 2024) Subject: First-aid training for citizens The provision of first aid plays an exceptionally important role in the rapid response to emergencies and accidents and can literally save lives. However, there is little instruction or awareness-raising. The absence of a uniform training plan becomes even more apparent if we compare the different approaches taken by Member States. On the basis of the above and my previous question Ε-008747-15 (1): 1.
Does the Commission have detailed data on first-aid training for citizens, and if so, what is the situation in Greece?

How does it plan to raise awareness among citizens and give them incentives to take appropriate training, and what financial tools can be made available to promote similar education in school curricula?
How does the Commission intend to standardise first-aid training methods in Member States with the aim of ensuring the highest possible quality?

(17 June 2024) As the Commission mentioned in its reply to written question Ε-008747/15, the responsibility for first-aid training, organisation of medical care and emergency response lies with the Member States. Therefore, the Commission does not keep information on citizen first-aid training or its harmonisation. However, through the Union Civil Protection Mechanism (2) (UCPM), the Commission facilitates cooperation between Member States in the field of disaster prevention, preparedness and response. The Commission has set up the disaster resilience goals (3) as non-binding recommendations to identify areas to strengthen the resilience of the UCPM and of the Member States. The second goal ‘prepare’ specifically recommends that the EU and Member States’ authorities should ensure that the population can easily access information on disaster risks. Public authorities and other organisations may apply for EU funding for projects aimed at raising awareness of disaster risks and improving training in disaster response procedures. Examples include the Knowledge for Action in Prevention and Preparedness (4) and Technical Assistance for Disaster Risk Management (5) grants. Between 2021-2027, the Greek thematic programme on civil protection has allocated over EUR 28 million to improve the capacity of the population, including students, to deal with disasters through awareness-raising. This includes, for example, publication of informative materials and implementation of preparedness exercises.
